newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia, Japan disagree on cause of tanker accident.
newsitem.headline: Russia, Japan disagree on cause of tanker accident.

text.p: Russian and Japanese authorities cannot agree on what caused the Russian tanker Nakhodka to sink last month, causing widespread pollution off the Japanese coast, Russia's transport minister said on Friday.

Nikolai Tsakh told a news conference that Moscow continues to believe "an external cause" is to blame for the huge ship breaking in two. Japanese officials estimate it spilt 5,000 tonnes of oil into the sea off Japan.
The Russian commission last month determined that the tanker had been in good condition but split up and sank after hitting a half-submerged ship in heavy seas.
"The nose of the tanker split off...but a tanker's front can't usually just fall off," Tsakh said on Friday. "That is why the Russian commission came to this conclusion."

Japanese officials believe a combination of stormy weather and the advanced age of the tanker, launched more than 25 years ago, caused the accident. The disaster led to the worst oil spill in Japanese history, polluting the coast and affecting important fishing areas.
Russia and Japan agreed to form a joint committee of maritime experts late last month to study the accident, and both sides say that this work is continuing.
"The word disagreement is not appropriate at this stage," said Takashi Kurai, political counsellor at the Japanese Embassy in Moscow. "We are now in the process of finding out the cause."

The January 2 accident will cost insurers about $500 million overall, Tsakh said. The owner of the tanker, Prisco Traffic Ltd. in Nakhodka in Russia's Far East, has promised to reimburse Japan fully for the environmental disaster.
